facts.text: Midtown Miami grew from a former Florida East Coast Railway yard into a mixed‑use district with high‑rise apartments and a planned shopping hub.
Only two residential towers and about two‑thirds of the original retail plan were completed before the 2007 real‑estate crash halted the rest of Midtown’s development.
In 2011, Midtown announced a new entertainment center that would add a hotel and shops to the temporary park at the district’s core.
Midtown’s outdoor shopping area, called The Shops at Midtown, was designed to echo New York’s SoHo neighborhood and hosts a mix of national and local retailers.
The district also became a venue for Art Miami, an art fair that runs during Miami’s Art Basel week and draws international collectors.
Midtown’s development began in 2005, when construction started on the site between North 29th and 36th Streets and Miami Avenue, marking the first major urban renewal effort in the area.
